# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report
> through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: US-UPD-01 (United States)
- Period: week 12 (starting 2026-03-23)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift estimates that the AI's catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) at this clinic dropped to 67% (band 48% to 85%), against a baseline of 90%. This estimate is predicted from 50 scans from this week alone; expert reference grades for these scans have not yet arrived.

## 4. Potential patient impact
If the estimate is correct, approximately 3.03485 referable cases may have been missed. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
A shift in the screened patient population towards lower-risk individuals is considered the most probable cause, though the evidence remains weak due to the limited sample size of 50 scans. The referral rate fell sharply, whereas image quality metrics remained largely stable. (category: patient population shift; confidence 60%; source: gemini)

Evidence:
- Referral rate decreased by -61.4%, from 0.414 in training to 0.16 at the clinic.
- Image quality remained largely unchanged, with mean quality at 0.871 compared to 0.875 in training (-0.5% relative change).
- Mean contrast showed minimal change, moving from 0.0893 to 0.0891 (-0.2% relative change), and mean brightness shifted slightly from 0.402 to 0.382 (-4.8% relative change).
- Mean resolution was unchanged at 1020.0 px (0.0% relative change), whilst mean sharpness decreased slightly from 31.8 to 28.5 (-10.2% relative change).
- Classifier referral score mean fell from 0.22 to 0.207 (-6.2% relative change).
- The weekly sample size is small at 50 scans, resulting in an estimated catch rate of 67% with a wide uncertainty band of 48%-85% against the 90% baseline, which limits the strength of the evidence.

## 6. Action
Expected harm: 117817. Cost of review: 25000.
As the expected harm exceeds the cost of review, it is recommended that deployment of the AI be paused at this clinic and scans redirected to human grading until the following checks are completed.

Checks:
- [ ] Verify patient demographics and intake criteria at clinic US-UPD-01 during week 12 to identify any shift towards lower-risk or healthier cohorts.
- [ ] Audit clinical triage and appointment scheduling logs for any recent modifications to screening indications.
- [ ] Monitor scan volume and referral statistics over subsequent weeks to assess whether this pattern persists across a larger sample size.

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alarm forms part of ongoing monitoring of the device in use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any model change made in response should fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: see recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
